name: Wings
s: The sky's the limit when estranged brothers - Joe and Brian Hackett reunite to run a commuter airline together. On the small island of Nantucket, the Hacketts run with a first-class crew of neighbors and co-workers, including lunch counter manager and childhood friend Helen Chappel. Their rival Roy Biggins keeps them on their guard, while sharp-tongued ex-stewardess Fay keeps them on their toes. …

paragraphs.text: Wings is an American television sitcom that ran for eight seasons on NBC from April 19, 1990, to May 21, 1997, for a total of 172 episodes.

The show is set at the fictional "Tom Nevers Field" airport, a small two-airline airport in Nantucket, Massachusetts (not to be confused with the actual Nantucket Memorial Airport), where brothers and pilots Joe and Brian Hackett operate Sandpiper Air, a single-plane airline. The majority of the episodes are set in the airport.

Tim Daly and Steven Weber star as Joe and Brian. Crystal Bernard plays Helen, their friend since childhood and later Joe's love interest and wife, who runs the airport's lunch counter but dreams of becoming a concert cellist. David Schramm plays Roy Biggins, who runs a competing airline, Aeromass. Rebecca Schull plays Fay, Joe and Brian's employee at Sandpiper Air. Thomas Haden Church portrayed the mechanic Lowell in the first six seasons, Tony Shalhoub was taxi driver Antonio from season 3 onward, and Farrah Forke was Brian's love interest, Alex, during seasons 4 and 5. Serving as the second spin-off of the sitcom Cheers, Wings was created and produced by Cheers veterans David Angell, Peter Casey, and David Lee. The trio later created the sitcom Frasier, which was also a spin-off of Cheers. Wings exists in the same fictional universe as Cheers, and many characters from Cheers occasionally make special guest appearances on Wings. The series was produced by Grub Street Productions, in association with Paramount Network Television.

Brothers Joe and Brian Hackett own Sandpiper Air, a small single-plane airline on Nantucket Island. Although both adept pilots who take their vocation seriously, Joe is type A and rigid, while Brian is a “free spirit” whose casual approach to life cost him a position with NASA in his youth. Regardless, he takes flying seriously, and is the only pilot Joe trusts.

Joe and Brian’s childhood friend, the beautiful Helen Chappel, runs the airport’s lunch counter. She has always been in love with elder brother Joe, while Brian has always harbored secret feelings for her. Helen’s refusal to date pilots (based on their perceived untrustworthiness), and Brian and Joe’s efforts to circumvent this restriction, are a common source of humor in early seasons. Helen's dream is to play the cello in an orchestra, and she attends auditions when not making sandwiches; Brian and Joe’s transport of Helen using the Sandpiper plane occasionally leads to misadventure. Fay Cochran, a sweet but scatterbrained widow, runs the Sandpiper ticket counter and is Joe’s best friend, often acting as the voice of reason when he comes into conflict with other characters. Lowell Mather is the dimwitted yet technically proficient airport mechanic, who maintains the planes for both Aeromass and Sandpiper while dealing with his chronically unfaithful wife, Bunny, who cares for the pair’s house boat. Bunny’s infidelities eventually lead to the pair’s divorce. Lowell leaves the island shortly thereafter, entering the witness protection program after he witnesses a Mafia assassination on the mainland and begins to fear for his safety.
